Definition: any notable constellation; specifically Orion (as if a burly one)
BiblicalUsage: Keciyl means Orion, the great constellation, the burly one in the sky: Job 9:9 says God maketh Arcturus, Orion, and Pleiades, and the chambers of the south. Job 38:31 asks, canst thou loose the bands of Orion? Isaiah 13:10 says the stars of heaven and the constellations thereof shall not give their light. Amos 5:8 says seek him that maketh the seven stars and Orion, and turneth the shadow of death into the morning.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Orion is God's handwriting in the night sky: he made it, he binds it, and he can darken it when he judges. I hold that the one who made the stars is the one to seek, because he turns death's shadow into morning.
